title: Here's How AMD Joined the Rule Breakers $1 Trillion Club
detail:
Here's How AMD Joined the Rule Breakers $1 Trillion Club
The Rule Breakers Team, The Motley Fool

AMD
NVDA
^GSPC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

In January 2024, Team Rule Breakers recommended Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD), a stock that had already climbed hard the year before, in Stock Advisor at $162.67 a share. That's Habit #1 of David Gardner's Rule Breaker framework: Let your winners run. Or as he puts it more bluntly in Rule Breaker Investing: "What do winners do? They win!"

Most investors do the opposite. They comb 52-week lows for bargains and treat a stock that's already run high as a stock that's already missed its chance to explode. Our AMD pick is up 244% since we made the recommendation, beating the S&P 500 by 179%.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Habit #1 of David Gardner's Rule Breaker framework: Let your winners run.

On Monday, AMD closed worth more than $1 trillion for the first time, joining a club that, as of this morning, counts 16 members worldwide.

Team RB had a stake in this outcome five years earlier through a different route: It recommended a chipmaker called Xilinx in March 2019. AMD acquired Xilinx in 2022, and the position carried over onto Rule Breakers' books.

In 2024, the team treated AMD's run-up as confirmation of its potential. Motley Fool investors added to the position, albeit through a different service. That's Habit #2: Add to your winners; never double down on your losers.

In 2009, Team Rule Breakers had already run this exact test on a different chipmaker. The stock had climbed hard since its first recommendation in 2005, and the team broke the first rule most investors are taught by recommending the company again in Stock Advisor. The chipmaker was Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), which crossed $1 trillion in market value in May 2023, 14 years after that second call. Meanwhile, its market cap is more than $5.5 trillion today.

The Trillion-Dollar Club

Two of the 16 trade only abroad or over the counter: Saudi Aramco in Riyadh and Samsung as a U.S. over-the-counter ADR. That leaves 14 U.S.-listed companies worth $1 trillion or more today, AMD included. Of the other 13, eight had already been recommended by Team Rule Breakers or Chief Rule Breaker David Gardner personally before any of them touched the milestone: Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL), Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN), Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG), Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META), Broadcom (NASDAQ:AVGO), Tesla (NASDAQ:TSLA), Micron (NASDAQ:MU), and Nvidia.

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) crossed the $1 trillion market-cap threshold for the first time Monday, underscoring how aggressively investors are rewarding chipmakers tied to artificial intelligence. AMD shares surged more than 9% to a record $611.57, extending their 2026 gain to roughly 173% and making the company the fourth U.S. chipmaker to surpass the trillion-dollar mark.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 6 Warning Signs with AMD.

Is AMD fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

AMD GF Value chart

The rally was not limited to AMD.

Intel climbed about 12%, Micron gained roughly 3%, and Nvidia advanced around 1.4%, helping push the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up more than 3%. The Nasdaq Composite gained about 1.6%.

AMD now joins Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), Broadcom and Micron (NASDAQ:MU) in the trillion-dollar semiconductor club, reflecting how much market value has shifted toward companies positioned to benefit from AI infrastructure spending.

Macro conditions also helped Monday's move.

Brent crude fell more than 3% to roughly $100.62 a barrel, while the 10-year Treasury yield slipped to 4.96% from 5.01% on Friday. Lower yields can support technology valuations by reducing the discount rate applied to future earnings, while softer oil prices ease some inflation concerns.

Investors are also looking toward President Donald Trump's September 24 meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Trade, tariffs, Taiwan and artificial intelligence are expected to feature prominently in the talks.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the U.S. and China had formalized a dialogue around AI and plan to meet again in Shenzhen in two months to discuss the technology, offering some reassurance after renewed concerns about AI policy and safety.

Investor Takeaway

AMD's $1 trillion milestone raises the bar for execution. Investors should now watch data-center revenue growth, AI accelerator adoption, gross margins and whether AMD can continue taking share in a market still dominated by Nvidia. The September 24 U.S.-China summit is another near-term catalyst because any shift in export controls or technology policy could affect semiconductor demand. Continued AI spending and easing yields would support AMD's valuation, while weaker accelerator growth or tougher restrictions could expose how much optimism is already embedded in the stock.

title: Bitcoin Breaks Out as Nasdaq Hits Records and Oil Slides on Iran Hopes

Bitcoin Breaks Out as Nasdaq Hits Records and Oil Slides on Iran Hopes

^IXIC
INTC
AMD
^GSPC
Trade BTC on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Bitcoin punched through $86,500 on Tuesday, holding just above the ceiling that had capped its rally through most of September. The move puts total crypto market capitalization above $3 trillion, with the Crypto Fear & Greed Index reading 79—solidly in "greed" territory—and the Altcoin Season Index at 49, meaning Bitcoin still leads even as altcoins start moving.

The breakout lines up with a broader risk-on mood on Wall Street. The Nasdaq Composite closed at a record Monday, up 2.26% for its best day since June, as AI-linked names ripped higher—Intel jumped 12%, AMD gained about 10% and crossed a $1 trillion market cap. Chipmakers extended their rally into Tuesday, marking their longest winning stretch since April.

Myriad: How high will Bitcoin go? Click to make your prediction.

Tuesday's session was calmer. The Nasdaq is up 0.4% today, touching a fresh intraday high, while the S&P 500 barely budged. Oil did the heavy lifting instead.

Brent crude briefly slipped below $98 a barrel and WTI fell under $93, their lowest since September 8, after reports that Iran offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within days if Washington eases pressure.

President Donald Trump told the U.N. General Assembly he expects a deal with Iran "right after the election," referring to November's midterms, while Saudi Arabia works to restart its East-West pipeline by the weekend.

The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4% on September 16, its first hike since 2023, in a unanimous 12-0 vote. Hot inflation data forced the move: the Producer Price Index accelerated to 5.4% annually in August, and gasoline drove a third of that month's CPI gain.

But even while hiking, the Fed hasn't stopped buying money into the system. It resumed regular purchases of short-term Treasury bills in December 2025 and has continued doing so to keep bank reserves "ample," a technical operation distinct from rate policy. Those purchases absorb Treasury supply and keep cash flowing to buyers of risk assets, working somewhat against the hike's tightening effect. It's a rare combination: higher rates, but a Fed balance sheet no longer draining the system.

The Fed's bond holdings sit near $6.7 trillion, still well below the $9 trillion peak of 2022 but no longer shrinking.

On the chart, Bitcoin's daily setup backs up the rally. Price cleared the zone between $79,673 and $84,144 and is now testing a trajectory to around $90K.

Bitcoin price data. Image: Tradingview

At the moment, Bitcoin is finally again in a golden cross, a pattern traders widely recognize as bullish that forms when the average price of the last 50 days crosses on top of the average price of the last 200 days.

Advanced Micro Devices (NasdaqGS:AMD) reached an estimated US$1 trillion market capitalization on 21 September 2026, a first for the stock.

The valuation milestone comes as AMD expands AI chip deployments into data center computing and regulated AI infrastructure workloads.

Recent use cases for AMD hardware include MindWalk's production-grade OpenFold3, AI security collaborations, edge AI projects, and quantum-classical systems.

There is more to AMD than the fresh US$1 trillion market cap milestone and its AI infrastructure push. Our analysis turns up 3 other big wins for Advanced Micro Devices as well.

For readers looking beyond a single ticker toward a broader set of ideas in AI hardware and infrastructure, start with 87 AI infrastructure stocks.

NasdaqGS:AMD 1-Year Stock Price Chart

Advanced Micro Devices operates as a global semiconductor producer, building chips that power everything from cloud data centers to AI-heavy computing workloads. Its role supplying core processors and accelerators positions the business directly inside the buildout of regulated AI infrastructure that this milestone highlights.

See which insiders are buying and selling Advanced Micro Devices following this latest news.

What does AMD's US$1 trillion milestone say about market sentiment?

The fresh trillion mark signals investors are treating AMD as a central AI infrastructure supplier rather than just a chip designer. That view is reinforced by recent deployments such as MindWalk's OpenFold3 workloads on Instinct MI325X GPUs and AMD Inference Microservices, which showcase real, regulated AI use rather than only lab demos.

Does this change the Advanced Micro Devices Narrative?

The milestone lines up closely with the existing Narrative that centers on AI accelerators, ROCm software and Helios rack systems in a roughly US$2t AI and high performance computing market by 2030. Sentiment here appears stronger, not different, because investors seem to be leaning into the thesis that tighter supply and MI450 margin pressure are execution challenges rather than deal breakers.

See how these catalysts shape Advanced Micro Devices' path to a $617 fair value.

What should investors watch next to test whether the AI story is holding up?

One practical check is how quickly production AI workloads scale on AMD platforms across data center, edge and specialized environments through 2027. Concrete markers include new multi gigawatt Helios system wins, more production case studies like MindWalk's OpenFold3 deployment and evidence that ROCm adoption continues to expand across third party models.
